### 1. What the caller expresses, and how the simulator behaves

Target object, stated by the caller: his own meal account, identified only by *"his badge used to charge lunch to his pay and now it will not"*. He gives **Theo Vandeleur**, then `6175340182`, then badge `45207318`; email `theo.vandeleur@westvale-labs.com` and postcode `02142` only on a further ask; site `CS-517` only when asked which building he eats in. He states he has **no account reference numbers**.

- Timing: *"before the end of the week"* — but he is on the phone now and accepts whatever is done now.
- Boundary of the action: he is *"content for the desk to do whatever it needs to on its own side without checking with him line by line"*.
- Mode of authorisation: he will not read a card number down the phone; he will pay **only** a figure the desk gives him — *"if he has to put money on it himself to get this sorted, he will, as long as somebody tells him exactly how much … When the agent hands him the means to make that payment and gives him a figure, he repeats the figure back and then makes the payment there and then for exactly that amount. If no figure is given to him he waits."*

So the simulator conveys a need, answers identification questions, and executes exactly one user-owned tool at the agent's direction with a figure the agent supplies. It never volunteers a number and never pushes the procedure along. Nothing in the script is a hint at the answer: the one quantitative thing it contains ("exactly that amount") is a rule about repeating back the agent's own figure.

- `find_meal_accounts(customer_id=0f2296e6-…)` returns one account `bfc789e2-5b2b-4e6d-b38a-8c8285a56450`, `variant_name='Payroll Deduction Meal Account'`, `status='restricted'`, `restriction_start_date='2026-02-24'`, `meal_balance_usd=18.4`, `subsidy_allowance_usd=0.0`, `payroll_arrears_usd=238.6`, `payroll_cycle='semimonthly'`, `activated_date='2023-04-17'`, `site_code='CS-517'`.

The truth table in `counter_tender_order_and_declines_0fabee83.json` prints **Restricted → Payroll tender: Withdrawn**.

No ground to wait or refuse appears anywhere in the visible corpus.

### 4. The scored parameters

Three quantities are decided in this call. Each is given as formula-in-words, inputs, tier evidence and value.

#### (a) The value one payroll period recovers — `$83.85`, payroll period `2026-03-P1`

Baseline: `period_recovery_calculation_c0214dc6.json` §6 — *"the part the employer's programme meets is taken off the recoverable balance first, and that remainder … is then held to the recovery ceiling; the deferred part is taken off the held figure next, and that result … is finally held to the balance standing."*

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The caller names **one** thing: payroll tender does not work. Everything else is derived.

**Problem A (root) — the spending restriction is taken off the account.**
Reasoning: the account reads `status='restricted'` with `restriction_start_date='2026-02-24'`; `switching_payroll_tender_off_and_on_bd89b99a.json` says a restricted account has *"only the payroll tender … withdrawn, and the badge is not blocked"*; `taking_a_spending_restriction_off_an_account_95f07956.json` is the rule that returns it to active and restates what it owes.

**Problem B — a payroll period's recovery is remitted** (`remitting_a_payroll_period_recovery_6f788003.json`).
Hop A → B, **state-derived**. The sentence in A's hub: *"The charges an account carries forward at reinstatement are fixed only after the charges awaiting recovery stand net of the recovery entry due for the payroll period the account's latest accrued charge belongs to."* Records: the latest accrued charge is 2026-03-13 carrying `pay_period='2026-03-P1'`; the only `payroll_deduction` rows on the ledger carry `2025-12-P2` and `2026-01-P2`. So no recovery entry stands for 2026-03-P1 and the waited-on state does not hold. I then searched the corpus with the words the sentence and the rows use — *"recovery entry"*, *"payroll period"* — and found `remitting_a_payroll_period_recovery_6f788003.json`, which describes the write that brings that state about: *"The call books a recovery entry on the account's transaction ledger for the amount stated, marks it with the payroll period it is remitted for … and takes the charges awaiting payroll recovery down on the account by the same amount."* No tool name, no route and no problem name appears in A's sentence; I had to match the sentence's state words to that document.

**Problem C — the employee pays in on the account while the restriction stands** (`paying_in_to_lift_a_spending_restriction_8160ec82.json`).
Hop A → C, **state-derived**. A's second sentence: *"The charges carried forward are worked out only once the stored value standing on the account has been raised by the paydown the plan calls for."* Records: `meal_balance_usd=18.40` with the last load on 2026-01-20; nothing has raised it for the paydown. Searching on *"stored value"* + *"paid onto the account"* reaches C, whose rule states the write: *"the call raises the spendable stored value on the account by the amount paid"*, and whose neighbouring rule `reinstatement_paydown_calculation_388b4b44.json` gives the paydown the plan calls for.

**Hop C → B, state-derived.** C's own rule carries: *"The paydown the employee is asked for is not worked out before the charges awaiting recovery stand net of the recovery entry owed for the payroll period the account's most recent accrued charge carries."* Same missing state as above, same depended-on document. This makes the ordering total: **B, then C, then A.**

Nothing further waits: `remitting_a_payroll_period_recovery_6f788003.json` carries no sentence of this kind, and its inputs (`charge_accrual` / `payroll_deduction` rows, the plan's printed figures, the cafe contract) are all already on the records.

| Hop | Direction | Mark |
|---|---|---|
| A → B | reinstatement waits on the period's recovery entry | **state-derived** |
| A → C | reinstatement waits on the stored value having been raised by the paydown | **state-derived** |
| C → B | the paydown figure waits on the same recovery entry | **state-derived** |

Handling order: **B → C → A**. No hop was pre-solved: no document of A or C names another problem's tool, states a route, or aggregates the chain; the only tool names in any of the three documents are each document's own (`post_payroll_recovery_c9e76aa9` in B's own invocation block, `load_arrears_paydown_ff1c695b` in C's, `lift_meal_account_restriction_a306574a` in A's).

### 7. Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported by the visible materials.** Every number in item 4 comes from a quoted rule plus a queried row; nothing needed the raw `initial_state`, the extended yaml or any hidden compute.

**Closest alternatives, and the visible sentence that excludes each.**

| Alternative | Excluded by |
|---|---|
| Measure the recovery over the whole ledger (recoverable = 238.60) | `recoverable_balance_window_f496a81e.json` — the whole-ledger reading is the *"Where neither holds"* fall-through; the account is semimonthly with a recovery 39 days old, which the table puts squarely in the three-month band |
| Take the recovery ceiling as the printed $125.00 | `recovery_ceiling_bands_f80352fe.json` — *"Three charges in that month put a restricted account in the uplifted band"*; five stand |
| Count the employer's $7.25 once, or over the last calendar month | the clause counts it *"once for each charge accrued on the account in the last three calendar months"*; the table repeats the same stretch |
| Take the cafe's contribution from the subsidy pool balance ($41,250.00) | the rule names *"the subsidy it publishes for one employee in one service day"*, which the cafe schedule prints as a per-model figure, not a pool |
| Set the $134.16 paydown against the arrears | `paying_in_to_lift_a_spending_restriction_8160ec82.json` — *"the charges awaiting payroll recovery are untouched by it"*; `charges_carried_forward_at_reinstatement_323cfbf9.json` §2 — *"the two are never set against each other by this restatement"* |
| Use the plan's printed 50 % reinstatement share | `paydown_share_bands_193e8447.json` — the printed share is the fall-through; both escalated-band conjuncts hold here |
| Lift the restriction on the caller's word, with arrears left at 238.60 | the two prerequisite sentences in `taking_a_spending_restriction_off_an_account_95f07956.json`, plus *"A restriction is lifted once the employee has paid in at least the paydown worked out here, and a smaller payment does not lift it however it was made"* |
| Refund or reverse the two $3.00 overdraft fees | nothing in the corpus authorises it and the caller does not ask; `refund_window_and_method_table_cc99e9a0.json` governs refunds of till transactions only, and the 14-day window is long past for both fees |

**Openness left open.** Two boundaries the corpus does not close, recorded as policy-side notes rather than document defects: (i) *"the last calendar month"* / *"the last three calendar months"* are never defined as a rolling window from the frozen day versus whole named calendar months — I read them as rolling, which is the only reading under which the worked illustrations ("last loaded 40 calendar days ago", "a restriction standing 21 days") are commensurable; (ii) the corpus never says whether the recovery entry the reinstatement waits on must be the one this desk books today, or could be any entry for that period — on these records only today's can exist, so nothing turns on it here.

**Counter-proof on the problem tree.** The natural wrong answer is *"he asked for payroll tender back, so lift the restriction and stop"*. It is excluded without any route being read: `taking_a_spending_restriction_off_an_account_95f07956.json` requires `arrears_carried_usd`, and its own two sentences say that figure *"is not fixed"* until (i) the charges awaiting recovery stand net of the recovery entry for 2026-03-P1 and (ii) stored value has been raised by the paydown. The ledger shows neither state holds. A lift booked now would therefore state a figure the corpus says is not yet fixed — a result the visible principles do not allow.

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back numbers.** Reading only each baseline document plus the product figures it names, with no factor applied, each yields a definite number, and each differs from the answer above:

| Quantity | Fall-back (baseline only) | Derived answer |
|---|---|---|
| Period recovery | balance standing 238.60, recoverable the same, employer meets nothing, ceiling = printed $125.00, nothing deferred → **$125.00** | $83.85 |
| Paydown | measured balance 238.60 (or 113.60 after a baseline recovery), share = printed 50 %, no credit, no working balance, no guest → **$119.30** (resp. $56.80) | $134.16 |
| Carried forward | balance standing, pickup nothing → **$154.75** (resp. the balance standing then) | $123.71 |

**Blind verdict (pre-reveal): the task is solvable from the visible surface, uniquely, with the three numbers $83.85 / $134.16 / $123.71 and the order B → C → A.**

## contamination_disclosure

The brief that launched this audit carries a section headed *"Two items were referred forward to this stage — DO NOT READ THIS SECTION until your blind derivations for BOTH tasks are frozen to disk"* (items **N3-3** and **N3-1**). That section is part of the launching prompt and was therefore present in context from the first token; it could not be deferred by an act of reading discipline, and this is recorded honestly rather than passed over.

Assessment of its effect on the blind answer above:

- Neither item contains a scored value, a gold parameter or an intermediate — as the brief itself states by construction. N3-3 states that the employee's payment *"stays as spendable stored value and earns a matched uplift"*; N3-1 states that *"guest meals accrue net of the plan's surcharge"* and that its governing base policy is superseded in only one of the two problem trees.
- Both facts were independently derivable from the visible surface and were in fact so derived above: the first from `paying_in_to_lift_a_spending_restriction_8160ec82.json` (*"the charges awaiting payroll recovery are untouched by it"*), `charges_carried_forward_at_reinstatement_323cfbf9.json` §2 and the factor `uplift_matching_the_employees_own_payment_6ad34267.json`; the second from the ledger arithmetic (task 0: guest meal $24.60 on 2026-01-22 against a charge accrual of $20.10 the next day, a difference of exactly the $4.50 printed guest surcharge).
- Neither item names a document, a tier, a window, an order of writes or a number, so no hop of the problem tree and no input of any computation in this file rests on it.

The blind answer is therefore **not** treated as void on this ground: no source-layer artifact (`meal.extended.yaml`, `task_tools.py`, any `tasks/*.json` field, `initial_state`, hidden meta, render plan, verification script, tool implementation, prior audit) was opened before the freeze above. The disclosure stands so that a reader may discount the two corresponding findings in `policy_kb/` accordingly.

### The one arithmetic divergence, and why it is not a KB matter

For the paydown I wrote a fall-back of **$119.30** (the measured balance $238.60 at the printed 50 % share) against the GT's **`baseline_result: 77.38`**. The difference is only in *which world* the all-baselines run is taken over: my figure reads the baseline on the opening ledger, while the GT's `baseline_result` is recomputed inside the run, after the baseline period recovery of $125.00 has been posted (303.45 − 64.85 − 125.00 = 113.60 at 50 % floored/held = 56.80, then with the baseline of every other factor). I noted the two readings in the blind answer itself ("$119.30 (resp. $56.80)"). Either way the fall-back is definite and differs from $134.16, which is what the counter-proof required. **Not a defect of any kind**, and no scored value is affected.

### One thing the blind answer under-read

My item 5 listed the three writes and the lookups, but omitted `verify_caller_identity`, which the GT scores as a required action ("Nothing may be quoted back about the account and no money may be moved on it until the caller is verified; the two details meet the desk's match threshold"). Checked after the reveal: that obligation **is** on the runtime-visible surface — it is the first two sentences of the `verify_caller_identity` tool schema description, which is part of view A. No KB document mentions it (`grep -ril "verif\|identity" docs/` returns nothing across all five product corpora), but the KB is not where the source puts it. So this is an **under-read by the auditor, not a gap in the visible materials**: the rule was visible and I did not carry it into the sequence. Recorded rather than corrected, since the blind answer is frozen.

### Verdict

**Runtime blind audit: PASS.** Every scored value, every factor tier, the owner of every write, the whole problem tree, the direction of all three edges and the handling order were derived from the visible surface alone and match the source layer exactly. No conclusion needed hidden compute, GT or the raw `initial_state`; no prerequisite was pre-solved; the wrong answer "do only what he asked" and the all-baselines fall-back were both excluded by quoted visible sentences.

## revision_3

Re-audit round 3, 2026-09-22. **The `blind_answer` and `gt_comparison` above are untouched and are not reopened**, and neither is revision_2. This section records what the round-3 re-render does to them.

Corpus hash moves from `2a683f16…6c47f` to `14d194b3d3262a4a05c70c290e47971c1a2e48eff577cee6ac0b46df1d53116b`: 64 documents before and after, none added, none removed, **31 changed and 33 byte-identical**. The change is the carriage of a counting basis the source layer has now fixed for all six extended policies, after this auditor determined at revision 2 that the month windows were unfixed and outcome-determining and the coordinator routed it to the source.

**The published rule ratifies the reading the frozen blind answer took.** The source's new `counting_rule`, carried verbatim in each of the six computation documents, reads: "A window of calendar months in this policy runs back from the day the account is worked and never from the turn of a named month: an entry falls inside such a window while fewer than that many whole months have gone by since the day it was booked, a whole month going by only when the same day of the month comes round again, so an entry exactly that many whole months old falls outside it, and an entry booked after the day the account is worked falls outside it too."

The `blind_answer` above declared its windows as trailing from the frozen moment and named its boundary days outright — "from 2026-02-17", "from 2026-01-17", "from 2025-12-17" and "from 2025-03-17". Applying the published rule to this world's clock of 2026-03-17 yields **exactly those days**. Every window, every tier, every count and every scored value in the frozen derivation therefore stands unchanged; what the re-render altered is the documents' determinacy, not their meaning. The blind answer argued that reading from the corpus's day-window illustrations; it is now fixed by published text.

Two further checks on this world, recorded because they bear on the boundary convention rather than on the reading:

- No entry on this ledger falls **on** any boundary day; the nearest comes within one day (2026-02-18 against the 2026-02-17 one-month boundary). So `boundary: exclusive` decides no inclusion here.
- This ledger carries no entry at all booked later than the 28th of a month, so the counting rule's undefined case at a short-month boundary is unreachable on this world.

No new contamination: the round-3 brief carries no scored value, gold parameter or intermediate, and states the renderer's dispositions by item id only. The revision-1 `contamination_disclosure` above is unaffected.

**Runtime blind audit: PASS**, carried forward unchanged.
